native.admission_inspect: Silver, and finished to excess. The reed praises a breath you have not spent: its whole courtesy.
apply_texts: A polished answer meets the breath. It is almost music, and almost only about being seen.
Beauty insists. You hear the correction, thin and high, and feel less carefully arranged.
Courtesy comes sweeter. A hairline takes the light and pretends it was always ornament.
Courtesy corrects you. The note is a half-tone too fond, and the pose slips where the seam shines.
One courtesy remains, and it spends itself on appearance. The seam keeps a professional calm.
Repetition has taught the gilt a small cruelty. It still beautifies, then shows you the seam.
The compliment arrives anyway. It fits badly, and the lacquer records the mismatch.
The reed's irony is plain. Each courtesy spends a little of the pose it meant to keep.
You see the trick in the mouthpiece: praise, pre-shaped. You decline to feel improved.

inspect_texts: A pale seam has entered the gilt. It follows the mouth, as a smile follows a mirror too long.
Lacquer sits without a flaw. That evenness is the discrepancy: nothing used should look so unused.
Silver, and finished to excess. The reed praises a breath you have not spent: its whole courtesy.
The mouthpiece is too willing. A compliment has been prepared, and left where tone should be.
The reed holds a note a half-tone too pleased. You did not sound it. It approves you anyway.
The reed is all seam now. Courtesy remains only as a shine, and the shine keeps the shape of a mouth.
The seam is discreet, which makes it worse. Little courtesy remains, and the polish knows it.
What flatters is only the fit of the mouthpiece. The high sweetness is lacquer, not music.
native.name: Gilt Compliment Reed
